Sprite naming and sheet reference

A schema and audit workflow, not an invented frame atlas.

On this page
What a verified row must containReported layer vocabularyDirection mappingTiming

What a verified row must contain

Exact ZIP path/filename/source pack, SHA256, page, layer, palette/variant, pixel width/height, action/facing, frame rectangle/order, source timing guide citation, compatible paired pages, pivot, import path, sprite/flipbook/sequence destinations, provenance and license restriction. Store unknown as null or unsupported, never as a guessed value that looks measured.

Direction mapping

Use four presentation directions until diagonal art is actually authored. Project movement onto the fixed camera ground basis, select the dominant component, and use hysteresis around boundaries to avoid rapid facing flicker. Retain last nonzero facing at rest; action facing may be locked for an accepted attack while motion continues under the action policy.

Do not mirror asymmetric weapons/hair by default. The missing northeast frame maps to an explicitly chosen existing facing, not a fictional sprite. Eight-direction production requires new diagonal body frames and every compatible layer/action, with re-audited timing/pivots.

Timing

Source animation timing is a visual starting point. Server cast/gather/cooldown/hit windows are separately authored gameplay seconds. A 12fps sheet does not define when a network reward commits. Clothing and weapons sample one shared body phase/frame; independent flipbook clocks eventually drift.

Planned game assets are not compiled assets. Values are proposals unless explicitly evidenced. Verification and limitations.
